meta.method: Google News RSS (en-AU, ko-KR), regulator page fetch attempts; Wikipedia/AUSTRAC page fetches blocked by extraction-backend + curl-pipe security denials. All claims below are headline-level evidence with source+date; items that could not be corroborated are marked [UNVERIFIED].

REG-FACT.status: headline-verified; exact current register size [UNVERIFIED] (AUSTRAC register page not fetchable in this run)

REG-FACT.claim: Case-level deregistration is real: AUSTRAC cancelled registration of DACSP 'GetCoins' following customer scam complaints; earlier AUSTRAC 'took action against 13 crypto firms'.

A dedicated VA/DACSP licensing-and-supervision framework (replacing pure registration) is in the reform pipeline and referenced in TRM's 'Beyond ASIC's No-Action Period' commentary — i.e., regulatory bar is rising for providers.

entry_read.australia: Rising: registration cleanup + licensing reform + AUSTRAC vendor-loop means budget exists, but TRM owns mindshare and Chainalysis-breach is an opening. Wedge: mid-tier DACSPs facing deregistration risk, priced-out by TRM/Chainalysis; OFAC-validator + 88k-wallet angle maps to AU scam-proceeds tracing. Caveat: exact register size and govt-contract landscape still unverified.
entry_read.south_korea: Sharper enforcement (record fines, travel-rule expansion) and bank-side demand (K-Bank), but harder market: incumbent exchange self-supply (Lambda256+Crystal), entrenched Chainalysis/Elliptic/TRM+CODE local partnerships, data-localisation/ISMS friction, and chainSENTRY's BTC/ETH/TRX/SOL coverage must prove KR-chain depth (KRW-exchange-linked chains, likely need Korean exchange API partnerships). Best wedge = post-breach security narrative + high-risk-VASP screening module for banks.
